def: A quick chain of stated assumptions and multiplications (users, requests, QPS, tokens, cost) that lands within a factor of two or three of the real answer, so you know what kind of system to build.
The ratio of peak traffic to average traffic, used to turn average QPS into the QPS a system must survive; around 2 to 3 for consumer apps, higher for spiky or working-hours traffic.
A measurable reliability or latency target, such as 99.9% of requests getting a first token within 1.5 s over 30 days; the gap to 100% is the error budget.
The share of support conversations an assistant finishes without handing over to a human agent; only meaningful next to the false-resolution and repeat-contact rates.
The share of conversations the bot closed as solved that were actually wrong or should have been escalated, usually measured by repeat contacts within a few days.
Retrieval that stores each chunk's allowed users and groups and returns only chunks the asker may open, so generated answers cannot quote restricted documents.
A prompting and training format where the model sees the code before and after the cursor and generates the missing middle, so completions fit the code that follows.
The probability that at least one of k sampled solutions passes the tests, estimated without bias from n samples as 1 minus C(n-c, k) / C(n, k) where c of the n samples pass.
The fraction of documents routed to a person because confidence is low or a validator failed; it drives most of the cost of an extraction pipeline.
The time from when a caller stops speaking to when they hear the first sound of the agent's reply; voice agents budget about 800 ms for it.
Deciding that the speaker has finished their turn, using silence thresholds and often a model that judges whether the sentence is complete.
The caller interrupting while the agent is speaking; the system must stop audio, cancel generation and truncate its memory to what was actually heard.
The share of items that truly belong to the positive class, such as violating posts; when it is tiny, even a small false-positive rate makes precision low.
A shared service through which every internal model call passes, handling authentication, routing, quotas, caching, logging and cost attribution.
Billing each team for the model usage it caused, based on tagged requests and an allocation of shared costs; showback only reports the numbers without billing.
